deadline.value: Nominal Fall deadline is 1 February; later applications may be considered.
deadline.quote: The nominal deadline for completion of the application for Fall is February 1st, though later applications may be considered.

app_fee.value: International applicants pay $60; US citizens and permanent residents pay nothing.
app_fee.quote: For international students the fee is $60

fee_waiver.value: Waivers are few; write to the Graduate Director with a CV to ask.
fee_waiver.quote: to apply for a limited number of fee waivers

gre_general.value: The department does not consider General GRE scores.
gre_general.quote: will not consider General GRE nor Physics GRE scores as part of our admissions process

gre_subject.value: The department does not consider the Physics GRE subject test.
gre_subject.quote: will not consider General GRE nor Physics GRE scores as part of our admissions process

supervisor.value: The physics page does not state a supervisor rule.

funding.value: Most students are supported by a teaching assistantship that covers full tuition plus a 12-month stipend; admitted supported students get 5 years.
funding.quote: Most student are support by departmental teaching assistantship that cover full tuition plus a 12-month stipend

also.quote: Admitted students with support are guaranteed 5 years of funding
Stipends for new students are anticipated to be $29,000

entry_route.value: A BS in physics, astronomy or a closely related field, with a GPA of at least 3.0, is the normal prerequisite.
entry_route.quote: The normal prerequisite for admission to the graduate program is the successful completion of a BS degree with a major in physics, astronomy or a closely related field

notes: PhD tracks: Physics, Astrophysics (Physics with Astrophysics Option), Biophysics, and Business (joint with Neeley). Interviews are held before admission. Catalog codes PHYS-PHD, PHAS-PHD, PHBI-PHD, PHBU-PHD.
